description: To introduce the core concepts and technologies that make web content understandable to machines.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: The World Wide Web, limitations of today's web, the next generation web, Semantic Web layers and technologies, semantics in the Semantic Web; XML basics, well-formed and valid documents, namespaces, XML schema, addressing, querying, Document Object Model (DOM), XML applications and limitations.

syllabus.title: RDF and OWL
syllabus.body: RDF basic ideas, RDF specification, RDF syntax: XML and non-XML, RDF elements, RDF relationships: reification, container, and collaboration, RDF Schema, editing/parsing/browsing RDF/XML, discovering information, querying (RQL, SPARQL), Web Ontology Language (OWL), classes, instances and properties in OWL, complex classes, property restrictions - role inclusion.

syllabus.title: Logic and Inference
syllabus.body: Rules, examples of monotonic rules: family relationships, monotonic rules syntax and semantics, Description Logic Programs (DLP), Semantic Web Rules Language (SWRL), nonmonotonic rules: motivation and syntax, example: brokered trade, Rule Markup Language (RuleML).

syllabus.title: Ontology Engineering and Linked Data
syllabus.body: Ontology types - logic, description logics, rules, inference and reasoning; ontology engineering: constructing ontologies, tools (Sesame, Jena, Protégé, NeOn), reusing ontologies, ontology reasoning; the web of data, shallow and deep web, linked open data, linked data principles and design, publishing, consuming and aggregating linked data.

outcomes: Understand and discuss fundamental concepts, advantages and limits of the semantic web.
Understand and use ontologies in the context of Computer Science and the semantic web.
Apply the RDF framework for Semantic Web.
Understand the concepts of metadata, semantics of knowledge and resource, ontology, and their descriptions in XML-based syntax and web ontology language (OWL).
referenceBooks: Paul Groth, Frank van Harmelen, Rinke Hoekstra, A Semantic Web Primer, Third Edition, MIT Press, 2012.
Yu, Liyang, A Developer's Guide to the Semantic Web, Second Edition, Springer Science & Business Media, 2014.
